# FAIR-bioHeaders in JavaScript

> Native JavaScript (Node.js) reader, validator and stripper for FAIR-bioHeaders metadata headers: FHR in reference-genome FASTA and GFA, FHP in protein FASTA, FHGFF3 in GFF3, plus an explicit opt-in rule-V7 lane that reads the FHT and FHGM drafts against digest-pinned bytes without making either one a support claim. It parses the `;~`/`#~` YAML header block, recomputes the SHA-512/256 checksum of the file's exact bytes, selects the JSON Schema contract the record cites (draft 2020-12) and validates against it, and can take the header out again so strict tools accept the file. No Python, no WebAssembly, no CPython-under-Pyodide: every check runs on Node's own `crypto`, `zlib` and `ajv`.

Key facts (this library implements the contracts released in FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification **v0.6.0**; it has no release, no npm publication and no version of its own — `package.json` says `0.0.0`):

- Schema versions it validates against: FHR `schemaVersion: '2.1'`, FHP `'1.2'`, FHGFF3 `'1.2'`. Which contract a file is checked against comes from its own `schema` URL, per the selection rules V1-V6; a release this build does not have is reported as `unsupported schema version`, never checked against a different schema.
- **This build retains historical FHT/FHGM draft pins and does not implement their released additions.** The shared project published FHT in `v0.7.0` and native FHGM in `v0.8.0`; those publications do not update this consumer. Native FHGM is distinct from the historical FHGFF3 extension read here. Its registry has no row for either addition. What exists is the reader lane rule V7 defines, which is a caller decision and not a capability that switches itself on: `inspectBytes(bytes, {container, drafts: ['FHT']})` recognises the pinned raw-main citation, `src/drafts.js` re-verifies the bytes against `drafts/provenance.json` (FHT: FHT-Specification `86438f21c3a17a58334c97aed4955be1a2393522`, sha256 `4156353aa6d077fee2d2c69be4e17859b8e4f81bb10824f3c87f6701de196e7a`; FHGM: FHGM-Specification `06176262f9824f26d974a15d8feeebde1fbeb0a8`, sha256 `b7075e5872e0a5ffce5ae61c590ce182f1f219fa269413cad3b1a966753cfeae`; the 2026-11-18 re-pin moved both contract byte sets and records the superseded digests in `previousPin` fields of the registry), and every record read that way carries a warning naming the citation, the commit and the digest, with `release: null` and `schemaVersion: null` on the reading. With no `drafts` option the behaviour is byte-identical to the pre-lane library (proved by `test/goldens/default-gate.json`), and a w3id or release-tag URL for either type is still "any other value" under V5. FHGM is not a header type: its records carry no schema and ride inside an FHGFF3 header under `x-fhgm-models`, judged in a separate block (B1, K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, K6; K4 resolves a `featureId` as written against the percent-decoded `ID` and `type` of the file's own feature rows by default or an injected resolver, and it remains no feature validator - SO terms, coordinates and biology belong to gff3-validator, and without a usable layer K4 is `not-checked`/`unchecked`, never a pass or a rejection).
- Acceptance is the shared conformance suite, not a local one: FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification's `conformance/` vectors (291 total, vendored byte-for-byte with provenance). Current result: **228 of 228 runnable vectors pass** (fasta 98/98, gfa 56/56, fhp-fasta 36/36, fhgff3 38/38). **63 are not run**: `jsonld` (37) and `microdata` (26) reader paths are not implemented and are reported as skipped, never as passes. The native test suite is accounted for, not just run: `node scripts/check-test-report.mjs` fails on zero tests, on a vector of the pinned manifest with no test, and on any skip outside the declared not-run set.
- Draft evidence is separate and labelled: the two development suites are run through the lane (`node scripts/capability/draft-vectors.mjs --fht <FHT-Specification checkout> --fhgm <FHGM-Specification checkout>`). Measured 2026-11-19 against the re-pinned bytes: **FHT 82 pass / 0 fail / 0 not-run** at the verified suite pin `86438f21` (manifest sha256 `e5a4a5d0…`, 82 vectors, whose contract rules carry the `C1`/`C2`/`C3` ids) and **FHGM 62 pass / 0 fail / 0 not-run** at suite pin `06176262` (manifest sha256 `e41f05fd…`, 62 vectors). FHGM stood at **58 pass / 4 fail** the day the re-pin landed (2026-11-18); the four were expectations FHGM-Specification#29 added to `layers.model` - K1 base selection by cited release (`carrier-cites-raw-main`), K4 root-gene-row target (`feature-target-gene-with-parent`), K4 raw-vs-decoded featureId identity (`feature-id-names-percent-encoding`) and K3 NFC-compared modelId uniqueness (`model-ids-equal-under-nfc`) - and they are implemented in this build (2026-11-19, Round 14 #23): the carrier must cite a registered FHGFF3 base release of the pinned overlay (raw main, v0.4.0 or a missing citation refuse); K4 targets only a **root** gene row, a `Parent=` or bare `Parent` token being indeterminate and rejecting, and row `ID=` values decode over raw bytes with strict UTF-8 so an un-decodable escape (`%FF`) is unaddressable while the record's `featureId` is compared as written; K3 compares modelIds after Unicode NFC, after the whole-record K2 pass and before per-record K4/K5. What a `layers.model` pass means is still the FHGM#29 reading of a **draft**: `FHGM#22`/`#27`/`#28`/`#32` remain open upstream and accepted decisions can move the expectations; and the earlier K4-abstention dispute this file recorded (issue #11) is closed by JS #20/#21 — a readable layer with zero feature rows abstains (`not-checked`), rows without IDs still score `not-found`. Eleven FHGM vectors reach K4, all against the file's own feature rows; a K4 whose layer is absent or untrustworthy stays not-run with that state as the reason, as does a vector whose `layers.gff3` expectation asks for a feature-layer judgement this library does not make. Four of the 82 FHT vectors carry `promotion: candidate-unreviewed` upstream and twelve FHGM ones came from a packet marked `Status: DRAFT`, so a pass on those is agreement with an unreviewed expectation, not a review of it; the runner prints that tally rather than leaving the counts bare. Every requested draft suite requires a complete pin; absent or partial suite provenance is refused before any vector or total is scored (issue #8, reaffirmed 2026-11-16). Each stated suite pin is digest-verified before anything is scored, and a suite that does not match is refused with exit 2 rather than counted. Those numbers are never added to the 291 and never described as support.
- The checksum is computed by `docs/FORMAT.md` R1-R5 and by `bioheaders combine` upstream — never by hand. This library can verify it and strip a header; it **cannot write or recompute a header into a file** (no `combine`). Use the Python toolkit for creating headers.
- Node only, for now. SHA-512/256 comes from `node:crypto`; WebCrypto's `subtle.digest` does not offer it, so a browser build needs a pure-JS SHA-512/256 that is not included. No browser support is claimed.
- Integers above 2^53-1 cannot be represented exactly by a JavaScript number; the reader reports them with a `precision warning` instead of pretending otherwise.
- This library is **not** the browser tooling on fhref.org and **not** `gff3-validator`'s Pyodide build. The family has ruled (fair-bioheaders.github.io#23) that the website's header validation must not be described as validation performed by JavaScript, because that page runs CPython under Pyodide. Nothing here inherits, wraps or replaces it, and those tools are not prior art for this package.
- This library does **not** validate GFF3 features. Syntax, sequence-ontology terms and biological consistency belong to `gff3-validator`; a valid FHGFF3 header says nothing about the lines under it.
- Rules it enforces are named by the shared identifiers: `R1`-`R15` (FORMAT.md), `P1`-`P2` (FHP.md), `G1`-`G3` (FHGFF3.md) and `V1`-`V7` (SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md); inside the draft lane, the drafts' own rule ids `C1`-`C3` (FHT) and `B1`/`K1`-`K6` (FHGM), K4 among them - it resolves against a feature layer and states `not-checked`/`unchecked` when it has none. Errors and warnings carry the rule id in the text.
- The published capability matrix is generated, not typed: `docs/MATRIX.md` comes from `src/types.js` via `scripts/make-matrix.mjs`, and CI fails when the file and the registry disagree. Every absent cell carries its reason.
- Licensed MPL-2.0, in `LICENSE` and in the `license` field of `package.json`. The `LICENSE` file carries the project's provenance split: historical USDA-ARS material stays public domain within the United States, contributions from March 2025 onward are MPL-2.0, third-party material keeps its own terms.

## Use

```js
import { inspectFile, inspectFileAsync, inspectBytes, stripFile, computeChecksum, selectSchema } from 'fair-bioheaders';

const reading = inspectFile('genome.fhr.fasta');       // {valid, container, metadata, checksum, schema, warnings, errors}
if (!reading.valid) console.error(reading.errors);     // nothing throws for a non-conforming file

const plain = stripFile('genome.fhr.fasta');           // Uint8Array, header block removed, every other byte kept
const big = await inspectFileAsync('genome.fhr.fa.gz'); // a stream: any size, gzip included, memory the size of the header
```

Install from the repository until a maintainer publishes it:
`npm install github:FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript`.
Requires Node.js 20 or later. ESM only.

## Repository

- [README](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/README.md): scope, API table, limits, what is not implemented
- [docs/CAPABILITY.md](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/docs/CAPABILITY.md): the dependency study — exact versions, why 2020-12, the ajv configuration the released bytes force, the SHA-512/256 proof, the YAML dialect findings and the JS number pitfalls
- [docs/MATRIX.md](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/docs/MATRIX.md): the generated type x operation x serialization capability matrix, with the contract-version table and every hole's reason
- [docs/CONFORMANCE.md](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/docs/CONFORMANCE.md): pinned vector source, per-format results, every vector not run and why
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for coding agents working in this tree
- [skills/fair-bioheaders-javascript/SKILL.md](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/skills/fair-bioheaders-javascript/SKILL.md): the same guidance as a skill
- [schemas/provenance.json](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/schemas/provenance.json): which release each bundled contract copy came from, with its SHA-256 — released contracts only, by rule
- [drafts/provenance.json](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/drafts/provenance.json): the rule-V7 pin: each draft's owning repository, commit and SHA-256, with `releaseTag`, `w3id` and `registryRow` null by construction
- [conformance/provenance.json](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript/blob/main/conformance/provenance.json): the pinned revision of the shared vector suite

## The standard, which is what to cite

- [FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification): released schemas, format rules and conformance vectors
- [Format rules R1 to R15](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FORMAT.md): header block placement, checksum coverage, encoding, `>`/`@` escaping, link schemes, extension fields
- [Schema versions and selection](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md): versioning policy and how a `schema` URL selects a schema
- [FHP](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FHP.md) and [FHGFF3](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FHGFF3.md) type rules
- [The shared llms.txt](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/llms.txt): the family-level summary, including the Python toolkit that writes headers
- Paper: Molik, Feltus & Yocum, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae122](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae122)

## Not implemented, not claimed

`combine`/writing any form, for every type; JSON-LD and HTML microdata readers
(the 63 vectors stay reported as not run, with reasons); JSON-LD expansion or
compaction; a command-line interface; gzip-writing output; browser or
Deno/Bun support; TypeScript declaration files; GFF3 feature validation beyond the
two columns (row `type` and `ID`) FHGM K4 resolves a `featureId` against; default
parent-link
recomputation for the released types (C3 runs only in the FHT lane, against parents
the caller supplies); the "near-miss schema URL" advisory warning that
fair-bioheaders 0.10.0 added; **support for FHT or FHGM at any version** — the V7
lane recognises a pinned draft, which rule V7 states outright is not adoption.
FHT and FHGM each wait on their own publication (`v0.7.0` and `v0.8.0`). Nothing is
published here either: no npm package, no release, no tag, no DOI, no registry
entry.

Agent workflow: use an explicit closing directive only for full issue acceptance; partial deliveries use Refs and remains-open wording. Read every overall/inline review, fix in new commits, reply to findings, resolve addressed threads and give an overall response even when there are no findings.

## Independent review and human-only merges (maintainer direction, 2026-11-20)

The [Round 16 policy](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/issues/211#issuecomment-7042896529)
supersedes the former conditional agent-merge authorization of 2026-11-16/18 and
the #268 authority links recorded under it. **Agents must never merge pull
requests in this repository; a human performs every merge.** Do not enable
auto-merge, enter a merge queue, use another agent or service as a merge proxy,
or push directly to the default branch as a substitute for merging a PR. Model
review never grants an agent merge authority; preserve platform protections and
do not forge approval or work around repository permissions.

Every PR receives independent review from another actual model. A different
model family is preferred (for example Codex or Gemini reviewing Qwen work, or
Qwen reviewing Codex work), but family diversity is a preference, not a hard
requirement; a second session of the same model is not another model. Record
actual author/reviewer model identities and never invent review provenance.

Agents keep monitoring CI and fixing failures and actionable review findings:
read the overall review and every inline finding, fix in new commits, reply with
disposition and evidence, resolve handled threads and acknowledge clean reviews.
Validate the current head after changes and hand the human exact head/base,
review, CI, dependency and remaining-risk information. Missing, failed and
NOT_RUN checks are not passes. This grants no contract adoption, curator
acceptance, release, publication or deployment authority — those gates are
unchanged. Earlier rounds' authorized merges and dated receipts remain accurate
historical facts, not future permission.
